conflicts.quote: product preference is that **any paid-book body class still living on the same app OLTP volume** also leaves that volume if it would otherwise remain the retention bottleneck.
conflicts.why: Read against live ring BYTEA still co-located on app Postgres, this preference pulls `ChainSnapshotStore` / `pg_chain_snapshot` body migration into this BRIEF whenever OLTP feels tight inside the existing 14d+48/symbol envelope. Architect’s named shape moves only prune-proof session-archive bodies (pointer index + FS/Railway-volume body store); ring non-move is an explicit non-goal because the ring is already bounded while session identity is unbounded by design. Expanding to a second body-store cutover is scope, not required by the session-OLTP failure mode.
conflicts.proposal: Keep this ship to session-archive body/index split only. Satisfy AC-22 by recording residual risk: ring BYTEA may still pressure OLTP inside the 48/14d envelope. A human Decision card is required before ring bodies become In.

conflicts.quote: **Silent ring deferral** — session bodies move, ring bodies still dominate disk, and the BRIEF "weeks can accumulate" claim stays false.
conflicts.why: That causal claim does not follow from the store split. Weeks of session corpus accumulate because session books are prune-proof and were retaining full chain BYTEA beside identity; moving those bodies off the app OLTP volume is the mechanism that stops Postgres disk from being session retention policy. The ring remains separately capped (14d + 48/symbol), so leaving ring BYTEA in place does not by itself falsify session-book accumulation for the corpus wait.
conflicts.proposal: Treat ring deferral as residual bounded OLTP pressure (AC-22), not as failure of the BRIEF’s session-retention decision impact. Ship-blocking ACs stay on session bodies off OLTP, zero-Massive list/load, and honest miss/unreadable/not-storing.

conflicts.quote: **`review` owns** absence of trader UI (AC-15), not raising 48 / not buying hist-chain (AC-19/20), program non-absorption (AC-21), explicit ring-body decision (AC-22), operator-without-trader-UI (AC-23), "authorizes: nothing" framing (AC-24), and Path-B same-store continuity at product level (AC-25).
conflicts.why: Trader-chrome absence and the hit-envelope `authorizes: nothing` field are negative space / wire invariants: a Settings row, `/_ops` storage badge, Ask-AI disclosure, or dropped `authorizes` key can land under an unrelated change while a review pass still looks fine. Risk-based verify assigns that silently-regressing class to `test` (structural `apps/dashboard` empty-diff + research-wire assertion) — matching UX AC-U1/U2/U13. Bundling them with intentional scope checks (no 48 raise, no hist-chain, program non-absorption, named ring deferral, Path-B continuity, positive operator-without-trader-UI) conflates two risk classes.
conflicts.proposal: Reclassify AC-15 and AC-24 as `Verify by: test`; leave AC-19–AC-23 and AC-25 as `review`. No DOM harness required — route/affordance negative assertion plus wire-field assertion is enough.

conflicts.quote: Operator-facing clarity may lightly touch research wording so `no session book`, `session book unreadable`, and `session archive not storing` stay distinguishable when object miss becomes common — but pixel layout, motion, and theme work are out of scope; my ACs bind operator list/load/desk observables, not screens.
conflicts.why: Those three strings are already the shipped closed set that keeps object-miss distinguishable (`session book unreadable: <reason>` for identity/pointer without readable body; miss stays miss; not-storing stays not-storing). "Lightly touch" invites a second deck or storage-backend synonyms ("object store miss," "volume unavailable," "off Postgres") — UX's defining failure mode and a direct reopen of session-chain-archive §4.
conflicts.proposal: Withdraw "lightly touch." Reuse exact shipped session-chain-archive §4 strings; map missing object onto existing unreadable; ban storage-branded rename strings. Pixel/motion/theme stay Out; `NO_UI_CHANGE` in SPEC §4.

conflicts.quote: When the object / volume store is **disabled / not configured / unavailable**, the trader desk remains available; archival does **not** report a false stored success; the operator can observe honest **`session archive not storing`** (or store-error) distinct from `no session book` and from unreadable.
conflicts.why: The parenthetical "or store-error" opens a synonym for the disabled/unavailable class and risks collapsing it into list I/O `session archive store error: <reason>` or into unreadable. Shipped vocabulary already separates not-storing (archive disabled/unavailable) from list store-error and from unreadable; AC honesty requires the exact not-storing string for this situation, not an equivalent class name.
conflicts.proposal: Bind AC-8's operator-visible outcome to exact **`session archive not storing`** when the archive/store is disabled / not configured / unavailable at open. Keep list metadata I/O faults on **`session archive store error: <reason>`** and missing/corrupt body on **`session book unreadable: <reason>`** — no "or store-error" alias for not-storing.
